moon_base/all.explanation: [PSI-99] SAFFIRE-II ranks highest (84.8/100) because its airflow matches the ventilated scenario, its solid habitat materials score a maximum 20/20, and it achieves a 10/10 richness score covering the prevention pillar. [PSI-98] SAFFIRE-I ranks second (84.3/100) with identical matching airflow, solid habitat material, and richness scores, trailing slightly due to an oxygen score of 25.3/35 compared to [PSI-99]'s 25.8/35. [PSI-68] FLEX-2 ranks third (77.0/100) because while its matching airflow and 17–30% O₂ range give it a perfect 35/35 oxygen score covering suppression, it scores lower overall (4/20 on materials) for using liquid droplet fuels instead of habitat materials.

iss_cabin/all.explanation: SAFFIRE-I [PSI-98] and SAFFIRE-II [PSI-99] rank highest tied with total scores of 93.4/100 because both matched the ventilated airflow scenario, tested solid habitat materials, achieved maximum richness scores, and closely matched the 21% oxygen scenario level. BASS-II [PSI-25] ranks third at 82.0/100 because, although its tested oxygen range fully encompassed the 21% scenario level and it covered two pillars, it received zero points for airflow due to unreported data.

spacesuit/all.explanation: SAFFIRE-I [PSI-98], SAFFIRE-II [PSI-99], and SAFFIRE-III [PSI-100] rank highest because they achieved identical top total scores of 49.0/100 (or 49/100). All three investigations earned full points in material (20/20) for testing solid habitat materials, full points in richness (10/10) for including experimental tables and 5 measurement types, and 14/20 in pillars for covering prevention. Additionally, each received 5/15 in flow due to ventilated airflow differing from the quiescent scenario and 0/35 in oxygen because tested oxygen levels either differed from the 100% scenario or were not reported.

moon_base/detection.explanation: [PSI-101] ranks highest with a total score of 65/100 because it covers the detection focus, matches the ventilated scenario airflow, tests solid habitat materials including foam and Kapton, and features a rich dataset with 109 test rows and 5 measurement types. [PSI-102] ranks second with a 64/100 score by also covering detection, matching ventilated airflow, and testing habitat materials like silicone and Kapton, though it includes a smaller 4-row table and 4 measurement types. Finally, [PSI-60] ranks third with 28/100 because, while it covers the detection focus, it only earns points for gaseous fuels and 2 measurement types while lacking reported airflow, named habitat materials, and an experimental table.
